models_evaluated: HD UNet 3D dose and uncertainty predictor (in-house)

openai.sample_unit: patients: 60 retrospective pre-implementation and 60 prospective post-implementation
models_evaluated: Hierarchically densely connected UNet (HD UNet) dose and uncertainty predictor

links.outcome: Radiotherapy plan achievability, quality, and planning efficiency with versus without AI-guided physician directives
links.effect: Achievability increased from 52.9% to 80.4%; first-plan acceptance improved from 63.3% to 90%; maximum iterations decreased from 4 to 2; four organs-at-risk had statistically significant dose reductions (range 4.3 to 15.2 Gy).
links.quote: As seen in Fig. 4 a, there is a significant increase in plan achievability pre- and post-AI guidance, from 52.9% to 80.4%.

links.outcome: plan achievability with vs without AI
links.effect: Plan achievability increased significantly from 52.9% before AI guidance to 80.4% after AI guidance.
links.quote: As seen in Fig. 4 a, there is a significant increase in plan achievability pre- and post-AI guidance, from 52.9% to 80.4%.

links.effect: The frequency of accepting the first plan increased from 63.3% to 90%, and maximum iterations dropped from 4 to 2.
links.quote: Fig. 5 demonstrated the frequency that physician accepted the first plan was improved from 63.3% to 90% and the maximum number of iterations reduced from 4 to 2.

links.effect: Testing on local retrospective data demonstrated non-uniform planning practices, verifying that the AI tool could potentially reduce practice variability.
links.quote: These results provide additional evidence that a reduction in practice variability may be possible via the implementation of the AI physician directive assistant.

unlisted_practices: Using AI dose predictions as an upstream decision support tool for formulating customized physician planning directives, rather than solely as a downstream plan optimization aid.
